newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - High offers into Taiwan tender.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - High offers into Taiwan tender.

text.p: Taiwan's reformate tender received high offers, reflecting the bullish sentiment amid tight supplies and strong regional demand, industry sources said on Wednesday.

Offers into Taiwan's tender for up to 500,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded reformate for March 1-15 arrival, were heard as high as $27.50-$28.00 per barrel, c-and-f. Taiwan's last purchase for February 11-28 was awarded at $27.00.
But sources told Reuters Taiwan was countering the offers which it considered too high. The tender which closed on Tuesday, is valid until Thursday.
Trade on Tuesday was comparatively lower, with 50,000 barrels of 95-octane lifting late February reported done at $25.20.
Bids for 92-octane were raised intraday by 40 cents to $25.40 and 97-octane by 25 cents to $27.25.
On a floating basis, 95-octane cargoes were talked around $2.50 per barrel fob, over Singapore naphtha spot quotes, although one cargo was said traded at $3.00.
"It is highly possible," said one trader on the deal, and who projected the differential to widen to as much as $3.50-60.
Traders said while February barrels within the region were scarce, demand was strong.
At least two majors in Singapore were heard seeking cargoes and India announced its tender to buy four cargoes of 25,000 tonnes each of 87-octane unleaded for first half March delivery.
"If India awards 100,000 tonnes in just half a month, it could be quite dry," said a major.
From early morning, two Japanese traders were heard seeking February lifting 95-octane cargoes, raising bids by 45 cents to $25.70 per barrel, fob by late afternoon.
Naphtha was well-supplied but edged up with crude. India offered another 27,000 tonne Madras low aromatic naphtha cargo lifting February 9-11 through a tender which closes Janaury 30.
February swaps were talked at $23.40/23.70, up 25 cents from Tuesday.
